title: Unicode normalization regression in canary causing tokenization aliasing - incident review
content:
Summary:
During a phased canary rollout of the v1.38 serving runtime on 2025-11-12 we observed a class of inference failures that manifested as truncated streaming responses and sudden decode exceptions from downstream consumers. Impact was limited to the canary fleet (~5% of requests) but reproducible across a range of inputs containing non-ASCII punctuation and certain emoji sequences.

What happened (high level):
- A config change introduced into the canary image enabled a new environment-level normalization step (ENV: LOCALE_NORMALIZE="NFKC") used by a helper string-cleanup library.
- The normalization ran before tokenization; for certain input sequences it altered grapheme cluster boundaries (e.g., compatibility ligatures, emoji + skin-tone modifiers) producing different byte sequences that the tokenizer mapped to different token IDs than expected.
- Because our model-serving manifest still referenced tokenizer metadata (vocab offsets) aligned to NFD-normalized inputs, the aliasing caused mismatches between expected token IDs and model embedding lookups for a small subset of tokens.
- Downstream effects: streaming encode routines encountered out-of-vocab indices and triggered a defensive exception path. Some generated outputs were silently truncated by the streaming proxy when the encoder returned nonmonotonic token positions.

Timeline (key events):
- 2025-11-12 09:05 UTC - Canary rollout started (v1.38 runtime w/ helper lib 0.9.3).
- 2025-11-12 09:22 UTC - First alert: elevated rate of decode-exception logs on canary (SRE alert).
- 2025-11-12 09:25 UTC - Observability: 0.7% of canary requests returned 5xx decode errors vs baseline ~0.01%.
- 2025-11-12 09:30 UTC - Oncall investigation: sample requests show token ID mismatches vs host baseline for unicode-heavy inputs.
- 2025-11-12 09:45 UTC - Canary paused (traffic switch to baseline). Immediate error rate dropped to baseline.
- 2025-11-12 10:10 UTC - Rollback of helper lib config in canary images confirmed; canary re-run with normalization disabled.
- 2025-11-12 11:40 UTC - Post-rollback monitoring: no further decode exceptions attributed to this cause.

Root cause (detailed):
- The new helper library behavior changed from no-normalization to applying Unicode NFKC normalization by default when LOCALE_NORMALIZE was set to "NFKC" in the service environment. This was introduced in a transitive dependency (string-sanitize 0.3.0 -> string-normalize 1.2.0) that was included in the runtime image build.
- Our tokenization pipeline historically expects inputs normalized to NFD (decomposed form) because the tokenizer's training data and vocab indices were generated from NFD-normalized corpora. The mismatch (NFKC vs NFD) resulted in subtle remapping of multi-codepoint sequences and ligature folding (e.g., canonical equivalence vs compatibility equivalence) which changed byte-level token boundaries.
- The tokenizer implementation is not resilient to receiving inputs normalized to a different canonical form: it does not check or annotate normalization form and the serving manifest does not pin a normalization expectation.
- Manifest & CI gap: the canary image upgrade path included the helper library change but no integration test covered cross-normalization token ID stability for a set of unicode regression prompts.

Why this only showed up in canary:
- The environment variable was only set in the canary deployment config used for runtime experiments (we inject LOCALE_NORMALIZE to evaluate upstream text-cleaning heuristics).
- Only a small fraction of customer queries include the particular emoji sequences/compatibility characters that trigger the difference, hence low but measurable error rate.

Detection and triage notes (oncall):
- Initial detection signal: count of "decoder::out_of_vocab" errors spiked in the canary logs.
- Quick triage: compared token ID sequences for identical inputs between baseline and canary; observed mismatches in token index arrays for inputs containing U+FE0F VS U+2640 sequences and a few ligature forms.
- Tested by running local tokenization on both NFKC- and NFD-normalized variants; reproduced the id remapping.
- Temporary mitigation: paused canary traffic and updated canary image to unset LOCALE_NORMALIZE, then restarted to validate.

Mitigation and rollback steps performed:
- Paused canary rollout at 09:45 UTC via rollout manager (traffic diverted to stable, canary instances drained).
- Backed out environment-level normalization flag in canary images and redeployed baseline image to the small canary shard.
- Validated token ID equivalence for a small set of regression prompts and monitored decode-exception counts for 2 hours.
- Notified product and applied-metrics teams.

Impact summary:
- User-facing errors were limited to canary traffic (no customer-facing outage).
- Potential risk if this had reached global rollout: subtle data corruption in embedding lookups leading to degraded generation quality and possible downstream log spikes or incomplete streams.

Contributing process/system weaknesses:
- Dependency/manifest blind-spot: transitive dependency introduced default-normalization behavior without an explicit manifest pin or an ops-config review.
- Lack of a normalization-contract in the serving interface: tokenizer and preprocessor lack an explicit, machine-checkable contract for input normalization form.
- Insufficient unicode regression coverage in canary CI: no test exercised emoji-ligature/compatibility cases across normalization forms.

Immediate follow-ups (owners & ETA):
- (Aisha) Add an automated CI tokenization-stability test that runs tokenization on a curated unicode regression set for NFD, NFC, NFKC, NFKD and asserts token ID parity or records differences, PR due by 2025-11-20.
- (Ethan) Add a manifest validation step in the image build that fails if any transitive string/normalization dependency has a default normalization mode enabled; short-term patch to image-builder by 2025-11-19.
- (Marisol) Add an explicit normalization contract to the serving API README and runtime config docs; define default expected form (consensus: NFD) and document LOCALE_NORMALIZE flag; draft due 2025-11-21.
- (Jared) Create an alert rule that triggers if "decoder::out_of_vocab" exceeds 0.1% of requests for any rollout stage; tuning and rollout to prod monitoring by 2025-11-23.

Longer-term engineering actions:
- Tokenizer hardening: update tokenizer to annotate tokenization provenance and optionally normalize inputs internally to canonical form before lookup; PR and bench plan Q1 2026.
- Contract testing: adopt a small corpus of unicode-heavy prompts that will run in pre-release gating and during rollout canaries.
- Dependency hygiene: enforce explicit dependency pinning for libraries that affect byte-level input semantics and add a dependency-checker rule for any package exposing unicode normalization APIs.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Do we make the tokenizer perform normalization internally (treat as implementation detail) or require callers to supply normalized inputs (explicit contract)? Pros/cons listed below.
  - Internal normalization: safer for operators, reduces caller burden, but may increase CPU on hot paths and hides upstream processing choices.
  - External contract: faster, transparent, but introduces fragility if env/config drift occurs.
- What should the canonical form be? Historically we used NFD; is there a good reason to switch to NFC/NFKC across the stack? (Product/localization input requested here).

Appendix: quick repro commands used by oncall:
- python -c "import unicodedata, sys; s='woman' ; print(unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', s).encode('utf-8'))"  # illustrative
- Tokenization diff: tools/token-diff.py --input-file samples/unicode-reg-cases.txt --norm-forms NFD,NFKC --tokenizer bin/tokenize_canary

Notes to self / informal observations:
- This felt like a classic example of a runtime/ops-level config creeping into text semantics. Need better guard rails around anything that modifies bytes before tokenizer.
- Keep the response small in the public notes; we'll include more technical detail in the postmortem wiki after we lock down the decision on internal vs external normalization.

Related artifacts:
- ENG-RUN-998 (rollout record)
- JIRA Redwood-5312 (bug ticket for tokenizer mismatch)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2876 (repro harness + test cases)

Status: in_review (collecting feedback from tokenizer owners and product/localization)
